notes_sections.title: Concept Clarity for Competitive Level
notes_sections.content: At Level 2, problems involve larger numbers, three or more numbers, and word problems. HCF (GCD) is the greatest number that divides all given numbers exactly. LCM is the smallest number that is exactly divisible by all given numbers.

notes_sections.title: Euclid Division Method
notes_sections.content: To find HCF of two large numbers, divide the larger number by the smaller. Then divide the divisor by the remainder. Repeat until remainder becomes zero. The last divisor is the HCF. This method is faster than prime factorization for large numbers.

notes_sections.title: Prime Factorization Method
notes_sections.content: Break each number into prime factors. For HCF, take common prime factors with smallest powers. For LCM, take all prime factors with highest powers. Example: 24 = 2^3 × 3, 36 = 2^2 × 3^2, HCF = 12, LCM = 72.

notes_sections.title: Three or More Numbers
notes_sections.content: Find HCF or LCM of first two numbers, then combine the result with the third number. Continue step by step. This reduces complexity and prevents calculation errors.

notes_sections.title: ₹ Based Word Problems
notes_sections.content: If ₹240, ₹300 and ₹360 are to be divided into equal packets, find HCF(240,300,360)=60. If three workers receive bonuses every 12, 15 and 20 days, they will receive together after LCM(12,15,20)=60 days.

notes_sections.title: Important Formula
notes_sections.content: For two numbers: LCM × HCF = Product of the numbers. This formula is valid only for two numbers.

notes_sections.title: Common Mistakes
notes_sections.content: Using product formula for more than two numbers, forgetting powers in factorization, and confusing LCM with HCF in word problems.

notes_sections.title: Quick Summary
notes_sections.content: Use Euclid method for large numbers, prime factorization for accuracy, and identify whether the problem requires grouping (HCF) or synchronization (LCM).

tricks.title: Fast LCM Using HCF
tricks.explanation: First calculate HCF, then apply LCM = (a × b) ÷ HCF.

tricks.title: Co-prime Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If HCF of two numbers is 1, then LCM is simply their product.

tricks.title: Stepwise Reduction Method
tricks.explanation: Solve LCM or HCF in pairs for three numbers.

tricks.title: Common Factor Extraction
tricks.explanation: If both numbers end with 0, 5, or are even, check common factors like 2, 5, or 10 first.

tricks.title: Large Number Euclid Trick
tricks.explanation: Use remainder repeatedly instead of full factorization.
tricks.example: HCF(221,391) found quickly using division method.

tricks.title: Multiples Observation Trick
tricks.explanation: If one number is clearly a multiple of another, HCF is the smaller and LCM is the larger.

tricks.title: ₹ Distribution Trick
tricks.explanation: Whenever equal grouping of money is asked, directly think of HCF.

tricks.title: Cycle Synchronization Trick
tricks.explanation: When events repeat after fixed intervals, use LCM.
tricks.example: Events after 9 and 12 days meet again after LCM(9,12)=36 days.

tricks.title: Power Comparison Rule
tricks.explanation: For HCF choose lowest power, for LCM choose highest power of each prime.

tricks.title: Option Elimination in MCQs
tricks.explanation: LCM cannot be smaller than the largest given number.
tricks.example: If largest number is 28, LCM must be at least 28.
